title: lucas-wu-all-hands-june-2026-q-and-a-draft
content:
Purpose:
- Draft Q&A and talking points for June 2026 all-hands (standing session).
- Focus: product highlights, customer wins, reliability/incident recap, hiring updates, roadmap bullets, and anticipated tough questions.

Audience: company-wide (eng, product, go-to-market, SRE, support). Keep answers concise and candid.

Structure notes (for presenter):
1) Quick top-line (30s)
2) Product & customers (2-3 min)
3) Reliability & SLOs (1 min)
4) People/hiring (30s)
5) Roadmap/what's next (1 min)
6) Q&A (remaining time)

Top-line draft script (TL;DR):
- "We had a strong quarter: Hosted API usage up ~45% QoQ, two new Dedicated contracts signed, and Private pilot expanded into a second regulated vertical. We shipped Optimize v1 (batching/cost suggestions) and improved median inference latency by ~12% across our model catalog. More on specifics in a moment."

Product & customer highlights (notes to speak from memory + link to slides):
- Hosted API: usage growth driven by mid-market PLG adoption and a couple of AI-native startups.
  - Note: emphasize improved token efficiency after Optimize tuning.
- Dedicated: closed 2 deals (one fintech, one ad-tech). Both chose reserved capacity + SLA.
  - Callout: Dedicated autoscale behavior improved; customer feedback: predictable throughput is the deciding factor.
- Private: completed pilot for a healthcare customer (HIPAA) in EMEA and started onboarding for on-prem proof-of-concept.
- Redwood Optimize: initial customers report 18-28% token cost reduction after suggested batching/quantization changes.

Reliability / incidents (candor zone)
- Recap: brief postmortem of May 18th partial degradation (KV cache eviction bug + autoscaling race).
  - Impact: 15-40% higher latency for 45 minutes for a subset of Hosted API routes.
  - Fixes: short-term mitigations deployed within 90 minutes; root cause fix merged and staged; improved circuit-breaker tests added.
  - Talking point: "We missed some automation signals here; we made changes to alerting and test coverage to reduce recurrence. We own it and learned how to surface similar regressions earlier."

People & hiring
- Hiring: hiring freeze lifted for Q3 headcount plan; prioritized infra/SRE, serving runtime, and sales engineering.
- New hires: shoutouts to folks who joined in May (list on slide).

Roadmap bullets (high-level)
- Next 6-12 weeks: rollout of Optimize 1.1 (more quantization profiles + model recommendations), Dedicated multi-tenant scaling improvements, GA of Private VPC control-plane for EU customers.
- Longer horizon: tighter eval integrations (auto-regression detection) and expanded APAC region availability.

Anticipated hard Qs and suggested answers (use conversational tone):
Q: "Are we still on track for our latency SLOs after the May incident?"
A: "Yes — median latency improved vs. last quarter overall, and the May incident was an outlier tied to a specific KV cache bug and autoscaler race that we've patched and added tests for. We also added a new synthetic traffic job to catch similar regressions earlier. Tracking this as a top SRE priority."

Q: "How are we balancing cost optimization vs. model quality when recommending quantization?"
A: "We treat quality as the guardrail: Optimize provides per-model suggestions with explicit quality checks (A/B evals on customer prompts). Engineers can opt into recommendations; we recommend progressive rollouts (canary, small percent) to validate quality before full rollout."

Q: "Any updates on enterprise sales — churn? pipeline?"
A: "Pipeline is healthy; we converted two sizable Dedicated contracts this quarter and churn remains low among enterprise pilots. We're investing in more sales engineering capacity to accelerate conversions and shorten POC cycles."

Q: "Where are we with security/compliance (FedRAMP, SOC2)?"
A: "SOC2 Type II is completed last year; we're making steady progress on evidence for higher assurance programs and have a dedicated compliance owner for Private deployments in regulated industries. For customers asking about FedRAMP: we have an internal roadmap but no public timeline yet — we escalate high priority requests case-by-case."

Q: "Are we profitable? burn?"
A: "High-level: we're focused on efficient growth. We're not public — we continue to balance growth investments with unit economics improvements (Optimize, Dedicated margin expansion). We can follow up with finance on specifics for managers office hours if needed."

Open/unresolved items (notes to action before finalizing slides):
- Confirm exact revenue % growth metrics with finance (placeholder currently says +45% usage QoQ — clarify if usage or revenue metric). [Action: Lucas -> Priya (Finance) by 6/10]
- Finalize list of new hires to namecheck. [Action: Maya -> People Ops]
- Decide whether to include slide with detailed postmortem timeline or only a brief summary. (Ops suggests brief + link to full postmortem doc).

Tone reminders (internal-comms guidance):
- Be candid on incidents. People appreciate transparency. 
- Avoid technical jargon when addressing the full company; use short explanations and link to deeper docs for engineers.
- Keep the Q&A answers short and leave room for follow-ups.

Backchannel / follow-ups to prep:
- Slack thread draft for #all-hands (announce agenda + link to slides) — Maya to post 24h before.
- Email to managers with FAQ and suggested ways to run team-level discussion post-all-hands.
- Postmortem link to share in SRE channel and attach to the all-hands notes.

Quick checklist before final PPT export:
- [ ] Confirm metrics with Finance
- [ ] Finalize hires list
- [ ] Slide deck visuals reviewed by Design
- [ ] Run tech rehearsal (10-15 min) with presenters

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Might add 1-2 customer quotes for credibility (request from CS).
- Consider shorter talking point on APAC region expansion — keep to one sentence.
- If asked about layoffs/posting: we have none planned publicly; recommend deflecting to private channels and refer to People Ops.

References / links to internal artifacts:
- Postmortem (SRE): confluence:INC-2026-05-18-kv-cache-eviction
- Finance metric sheet: confluence:rev-q2-2026-summary or jira OPS-4432
- Optimize customer case study (draft): google-drive:/shared_drives/product/optimize/case-study-pt1-draft

-- end draft --

(Notes: this is intentionally rough. After Lucas finalizes metrics with finance and hires list with People Ops, I'll convert to the slide speaker notes and condense to ~6 bullet answers for the Q&A slide.)
